text: {"final": {"findings": [{"id": "R1", "statement": "register_household(record: dict) -> Household in registry/register.py (line 36) currently validates only region, members, and duplicate ID: it raises ValueError for unknown region, empty members, or an already-registered ID. There is no validation of the household ID format/check digit, so a mistyped ID like HH-10471 is accepted and saved.", "file": "registry/register.py"}, {"id": "R2", "statement": "register_household saves only at the end: it appends the household to the loaded list and calls save_households(households) after all checks pass. Any ValueError raised before that point means nothing is written, so a new ID-format check placed before the append/save satisfies the 'do not save anything' requirement.", "file": "registry/register.py"}, {"id": "R3", "statement": "register_household does `record.setdefault(\"id\", next_household_id(households))` before validation, so registering without an ID auto-assigns one via next_household_id; any new validation must not reject this auto-generated ID (it is always valid, see R5).", "file": "registry/register.py"}, {"id": "R4", "statement": "Household ID format is HH-NNNNC: four base digits plus one mod-11 check digit (documented at top of core/ids.py). Weights CHECK_WEIGHTS = (5, 4, 3, 2) are applied to the four base digits in order.", "file": "core/ids.py"}, {"id": "R5", "statement": "Reusable validator: household_check_digit(base: str) -> int | None in core/ids.py (lines 19-28) computes the mod-11 check digit for a 4-digit base; it raises ValueError if base is not exactly 4 digits, and returns None when the computed check would be 10 (such bases are never issued). A caller can verify an ID by checking the format and comparing household_check_digit(id[3:7]) to int(id[7]).", "file": "core/ids.py"}, {"id": "R6", "statement": "make_household_id(number: int) -> str in core/ids.py (lines 37-42) builds a valid ID as f\"HH-{base}{check}\" and raises ValueError if the base has no valid check digit. next_household_id in registry/register.py uses it, skipping numbers whose check digit would be None, so auto-assigned IDs are always valid.", "file": "core/ids.py"}, {"id": "R7", "statement": "Example from the ticket: for base 1042, total = 1*5 + 0*4 + 4*3 + 2*2 = 25, check = (11 - 25 % 11) % 11 = 8, so the valid ID is HH-10428; HH-10421 and HH-10471 have wrong check digits and would be rejected by a check-digit comparison.", "file": "core/ids.py"}, {"id": "R8", "statement": "Existing tests in tests/test_registry.py call register_household(_record()) with no id (expects auto-assignment, test_register_assigns_next_id) and expect ValueError for duplicate ID and bad region (test_register_rejects_duplicate_id_and_bad_region). New validation must keep the no-ID path working and raise ValueError (or subclass) with the rejected ID in the message.", "file": "tests/test_registry.py"}]}}
